skill.name: allra-database-schema
skill.description: Guides Spring Boot database design for Allra projects, including JPA entities, QueryDSL repositories, DTO projections, and @Transactional usage.
skill.summary: Create consistent Allra database code with JPA, QueryDSL, entity design, and transaction rules.
skill.author: Allra-Fintech

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, Java annotations, QueryDSL fetch methods, and normal domain methods. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable shell logic, or unsafe network behavior was found in the reviewed SKILL.md file.

remediation.issue: Static scanner misclassified markdown examples as executable Ruby or shell backtick usage.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples clearly fenced and avoid shell-style command examples unless they are necessary and documented.

remediation.issue: QueryDSL .fetch() examples were flagged as network calls.
remediation.suggestion: Add short prose near QueryDSL examples clarifying that fetch() executes a database query through QueryDSL, not an HTTP request.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent Spring database code across entities, repositories, projections, and transactions. This skill provides Allra-specific JPA and QueryDSL rules for repeatable backend implementation.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Allra repository and Support interface pattern.
Shows how to place QueryDSL queries in the repository that owns the FROM entity.
Guides DTO projection design with Java records and @QueryProjection.
Defines when to use read-only and write @Transactional annotations.
Provides JPA entity examples with columns, enums, timestamps, and factory methods.
Recommends lazy loading and cascade choices for entity relationships.
limitations: It does not inspect live database schemas or production data.
It does not generate migrations or execute build tools.
Examples focus on Spring Boot, JPA, Hibernate, and optional QueryDSL.
Project-specific database choices may override parts of the guidance.

use_cases.title: Create a New Entity
use_cases.description: Apply Allra naming, column, enum, timestamp, and relationship rules while adding a JPA entity.

use_cases.title: Review QueryDSL Repository Design
use_cases.description: Check that custom queries live in the correct repository and return clear DTO projections.

use_cases.title: Standardize Transaction Boundaries
use_cases.description: Confirm that service methods use read-only or write transactions based on their behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Entity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a JPA entity for this domain object using Allra database rules. Include columns, enum handling, timestamps, and a protected no-args constructor.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Repository Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the repository and QueryDSL Support method for this search requirement. Place the query in the repository that owns the FROM entity.

prompt_templates.title: Review Transaction Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these service methods for @Transactional usage. Identify which methods should be read-only and which need write transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Database Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this database layer against Allra rules. Check entity mapping, QueryDSL projection style, repository ownership, transaction annotations, and relationship loading.

output_examples.input: User asks for a new User entity with status and audit timestamps.
output_examples.output: The response outlines the entity fields, protected constructor, enum storage rule, timestamp annotations, and a static factory method.

output_examples.input: User asks where to place a query that starts from User and joins Orders.
output_examples.output: The response recommends the User repository support interface, explains the FROM ownership rule, and describes the DTO projection shape.

output_examples.input: User asks whether a service method should use read-only transactions.
output_examples.output: The response classifies each method by read or write behavior and lists the correct transaction annotation for each method.

best_practices: Use the JPA repository interface as the service dependency, not the implementation class.
Place custom QueryDSL methods in the repository for the entity used in the FROM clause.
Mark read-only service methods with readOnly = true and write methods with a standard transaction.
anti_patterns: Do not inject repository implementation classes directly into services.
Do not place a QueryDSL method in an unrelated repository just because it joins that entity.
Do not omit transaction annotations from public service methods.

faq.question: Does this skill require QueryDSL?
faq.answer: No. QueryDSL is described as optional, and projects may use @Query or another approach.

faq.question: Can it run migrations or connect to a database?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance only and does not execute database or build commands.

faq.question: Which Java stack does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Java 17 or later, Spring Boot 3.2 or later, JPA, Hibernate, and optional QueryDSL.

faq.question: How should read-only service methods be annotated?
faq.answer: They should use @Transactional(readOnly = true) when they only perform read operations.

faq.question: Where should custom QueryDSL methods live?
faq.answer: They should live in the repository for the entity used in the query FROM clause.

faq.question: Does it define relationship loading defaults?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends lazy loading for associations and careful cascade settings for ownership relationships.
